items.title: Rossano Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 2, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So every time we heard one of these musicians playing we heard that there was something way superior... So we went to hear Tommy Flanagan in Milan... I went once all the way to Switzerland in Bern... to hear again the Tommy Flanagan Trio

ctx.x: Well it would be interesting to speculate if you could play a Beethoven piece when Beethoven was there and if you were taking more liberties than some other classical player, how he would respond to that.

Well some of the great composers used to be very much enthusiastic to see that their compositions was transformed by someone else. Other composers, they didn’t like that. But you see going back to the fact that I play classical music, I came up with this kind of desire. Like you know when we play jazz, we sometimes select a famous tune from the American songbook, and then we expose the melody and then we improvise on the tune. That’s what happens. And then after the improvisation you go back to the melody and…
In other words, you’ve got to swing it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
